precepts.text: Christ says the same thing: in vain they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
precepts.point: The elders of Isaiah's day had children, and those children became the Pharisees who opposed Christ with the same doctrines of men.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
Isaiah said the people draw near with their mouth and honour God with their lips, “but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”. The precept of men is the doctrine of men.

Christ says the same thing and names who Isaiah was speaking of: “Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

The elders in Isaiah's day were teaching doctrines of men, and the Pharisees in Christ's time were doing the exact same thing. Those elders had children, and those children became the opposition of Christ in his time. The same spirit passed down.

So the doctrine of trinitarianism is exactly that: teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. It is not found plainly in the Bible; it comes from men. People draw near with their lips and argue about essence and substance while their heart is far from God and they forsake his laws, and in vain do they worship him.

precepts.text: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
precepts.point: I will seek that which was lost: that's our people. And bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken: we were broken. And will strengthen that which was sick: we're the sick ones. But I will destroy the fat and the strong: I'm going to destroy the nations. I will feed them with judgment.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.” Who is that I? Christ. And Christ said who he came for: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

That is what Christ was doing, seeking out the lost sheep of Israel, and that is what Paul and the apostles were doing after him. That was the great commission in Matthew 28:19.

So when Ezekiel says “I will seek that which was lost”, that's our people. The lost sheep Christ was sent to are the same sheep God promised to search out and deliver “out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day”: all places, countries and lands.

precepts.text: Video played: a pastor declaring that the gospel cannot be for one ethnicity only, and that ministries teaching so are cultic. But Christ answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. It is one nation, twelve tribes.
precepts.point: Video played from a 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, filmed in Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family could live: residents said they would be afraid to go out at night, that you really could not trust any of them, and one said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march I don't like. They do not like when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
A pastor named Pam declared that the gospel cannot be for one ethnicity only, that it cannot be just for black men or for white men, and that this is a heretical doctrine preached by false, cultic ministries. Either the cultic ministries are right or Jesus is right; somebody is wrong. It’s you, Pam.

“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

It is only for one nation, twelve tribes. If you are not part of that, you are not getting in. Some of our people are bugged the hell out, and it is a direct correlation to slavery. A white pastor even said God blessed black Americans through white people and slavery, and Tatum agrees with that. But Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the same people under the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

precepts.text: So the scribes came down from Jerusalem. They started to follow Christ from region to region.
precepts.point: It says, then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees which were of Jerusalem: meaning they came from Jerusalem, following Christ around, from place to place. Cuz I said they follow from state to state; soon it'll be country to country. Don't be shocked.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
Matthew says “Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem”: they came from Jerusalem, following Christ around from place to place. Mark shows the same thing: “And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.”

The scribes came down from Jerusalem. They started to follow Christ from region to region, not to learn from him but to accuse him and call his power the devil.

They do the same with us. They follow from state to state; soon it will be country to country. Don't be shocked.

precepts.text: Then came together unto him the Pharisees and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem. Same thing done yesterday is being done this very day.
precepts.point: It says, then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees which were of Jerusalem: meaning they came from Jerusalem, following Christ around, from place to place. Cuz I said they follow from state to state; soon it'll be country to country. Don't be shocked.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account as Matthew 15:1: “Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.” They came from Jerusalem, following Christ around from place to place, gathering together against him.

The same thing done yesterday is being done this very day. Those who hate this truth follow these men the same way, from state to state, and soon it will be from country to country. Don't be shocked when you see it; the scribes and Pharisees did it to Christ first, travelling from Jerusalem to find fault with him.

precepts.text: The scribes and Pharisees asked why the disciples transgress the tradition of the elders, the oral traditions passed down, such as washing from fingertip to elbow before eating bread. Christ answered, why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? God commanded, honour thy father and mother; but they had a tradition where a child could say it is a gift, and be free from obeying his parents, like emancipation today. Thus they made the commandment of God of none effect: they were following traditions that contradicted God's laws.
precepts.point: Get your history right when you teach it: William Miller did not create the Seventh Day Adventists, he created the Millerites; it was Ellen G. White. Give the right breakdowns, or one day the enemy will catch you on it and embarrass you.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men”. To see what the tradition of men does, go to the scribes and Pharisees.

“Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” The tradition of the elders means oral traditions passed down. They had a tradition that you had to wash your hands from the tip of the finger up to the elbow before you would eat.

Here is his answer: “Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.” That is the fifth commandment, honour thy father and mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

“But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free.” The tradition was that a child could declare himself a gift and be free from obeying his parents. It is what they call emancipation today: America has the same thing, get to sixteen and get away from your parents.

“Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” The Pharisees were following traditions that contradicted God’s laws. That is the tradition of men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:8: whatever sets aside the commandment and is not after Christ.

precepts.text: But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Colossians 2:22 says the ordinances “Which all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men” Christ said the same of the scribes and Pharisees: “But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

That is why Paul calls the call back to the sacrifices the commandments and doctrines of men. Christ had come and taught the perfect way. Anyone still pushing the believers back under those carnal ordinances was teaching men’s commandments as doctrine, and that worship is in vain.

So stop following man. The ordinances of touch not, taste not, handle not were temporary and perish with the using; going back to them after Christ is worshipping in vain.

precepts.text: Honour thy father with thy whole heart: the root word for integrity is integer, meaning whole. And forget not the sorrows of thy mother: the fact that she carried you for nine months and birthed you. How canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee? You can't pay them back for bringing you into this world. So your responsibility as the child is to honor that alone.
precepts.point: And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. That's the judgment for not honoring your father and mother.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother”. This is not a commandment man stated; God commanded it. Honour means moral integrity, honesty and a strong code of conduct, a high respect, toward your father and your mother. “And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”: that is the judgment for not honouring them.

Sirach gives the measure of it: “Honour thy father with thy whole heart”. The root word for integrity is integer, meaning whole. Honour them with your whole heart. “And forget not the sorrows of thy mother”: the troubles she went through, carrying you for nine months and giving birth to you.

“Remember that thou wast begotten of them”. You came from them. “And how canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee?” How can you pay them back for bringing you into this world? You cannot. They did it because it was their responsibility.

So your responsibility as the child is to honour that alone: for nothing else but the fact that they brought you into this world and raised you. That is why our daughters are warned: the ones who walk away from their parents' protection for a boyfriend's sweet nothings can end up like the young woman sentenced to fifteen years, never to see that boyfriend again.

precepts.text: Glory not in the dishonour of thy father. Some of you who are older may have parents that are not in this truth, and you might think you don't have to give them the respect of a parent. That's not what the Lord said. My son, help thy father in his age: you are to be an aid to your parent at a certain age, and not just when you feel like it. If his understanding fail, have patience with him. Notice we're the only nation of people that don't take care of our elders; where do you think nursing homes come from? Deacon: I have a real disdain for children that do not honor their parents, because mine died when I was young and I went through the system with no mother and father. To have them, and be able to have a conversation with them, and still not respect that: that's a problem for me.
precepts.point: And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. That's the judgment for not honoring your father and mother.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Some who are older have parents who are not in this truth, and they might think that because their parent is not in the truth they do not have to give them the respect of a parent. That is not what the Lord said. It is no glory that your father or mother is not in this truth, and nothing to glory in because the Lord called you.

“For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father; and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.”

“My son, help thy father in his age, and grieve him not as long as he liveth.” You are to be an aid to your parent when they reach a certain age, and not just when you feel like it. “And if his understanding fail, have patience with him”. We are the only nation of people that does not take care of our elders. Where do you think nursing homes come from? The children do not want to deal with their parents at a certain age, so they pay somebody else to watch after them. That is how we honour our parents.

The Deacon has a real disdain for children who do not honour their parents, because his died when he was young and he went through the system with no mother and father, though his grandparents took him in. To have your parents, and be able to have a conversation with them, and still not respect that: that is a problem.

“And despise him not when thou art in thy full strength.” Be patient, because the example we set is what the young men see; we are their goalpost.

precepts.text: The multitude wondered when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see, and they glorified the God of Israel.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “the lame take the prey. And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick”. Jeremiah 31 showed the lame is Israel, and Christ shows the lame being made whole: “Insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.”

The dumb speak, the maimed are whole, the lame walk and the blind see, and they glorified the God of Israel. That is the lame of Isaiah 33. The lame take the prey: we are going to take the nations and divide the spoil, and in that day the inhabitants of Jerusalem will never say, I am sick.

precepts.text: Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing, and what is created more wicked than an eye? Therefore it weepeth upon every occasion. It starts with the desire of what you see, then the mind decides whether to feed the lust.
precepts.point: The brain stores everything: a random song from years ago surfaces because it is saved in long-term memory, the way your stuff never really leaves the internet. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and often we do not realize we are being controlled; you were made in a factory called America and those are not your words. The only way to break the code is to reprogram and recode.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye? therefore it weepeth upon every occasion.” The eye is where it starts. It starts with the desire of what you see, and then the mind decides whether to feed the lust.

That is why it belongs with Matthew 15. The Pharisees were arguing about eating with unwashed hands, and Christ told them that what goes in at the mouth goes into the belly and “is cast out into the draught”, but “those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.” What comes out of your mouth is the output value of what was put into your mind, and the eye is one of the ways it gets put in.

The brain stores everything you let in. A random song or thought from years ago comes out of you because it was saved in long-term memory, the same way your stuff on the internet never really leaves. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and a lot of times we don't even realize we are being controlled. You were made in a factory called America, and those are not your words. The only way to break that code is to reprogram and recode, and the wicked eye is where the guarding has to begin.

precepts.text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid? Job had to make a covenant: if it comes into my eyesight, I turn away. Netflix keeps it moving to hold your eyes, because the eyes are the portal to the vessel. Psalms 101:3: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes. Train your eyes to click past the enticing scene, and leave the conversation when the gossip starts, because three seconds of it will taint you.
precepts.point: The brain stores everything: a random song from years ago surfaces because it is saved in long-term memory, the way your stuff never really leaves the internet. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and often we do not realize we are being controlled; you were made in a factory called America and those are not your words. The only way to break the code is to reprogram and recode.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” Job had to literally make a covenant: I'm not going to watch that, and if it gets within my eyesight, I got to turn away. I got to train my eyes to look away.

That is the three-second rule. The eyes are input. If you let yourself look at something for more than three seconds, it goes into your working memory, your short-term memory; keep looking at it and you are programming yourself into long-term memory. Turn away within three seconds and it doesn't have time to work within your memory. That is why TikTok gives you three seconds to capture somebody's attention, and why Netflix keeps it moving: once they have your attention through your eyes, they have you. Our eyes are the portal to take control over your vessel.

The algorithm is a reflection of you. Your searches and your scrolls tell who you are, what makes you sad, what makes you mad, what music you play when you're angry. So when you say the algorithm got you, it's not them getting you. It's you, manifested on a screen. The devil don't make you do anything you don't want to do.

David said the same: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes.” Train your eyes. If a show is full of action but something enticing comes on that goes against your values and your struggles, turn it off, click by. If you hear gossip or something negative, leave the conversation, because three seconds of listening will taint you, and three seconds of something negatively influencing you will control you.

precepts.text: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
precepts.point: The prophets of Samaria, the northern Latino tribes, prophesied in Baal; the prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and walk in lies, from December 25 to the ever-virgin Mary, and strengthen the hands of evildoers so the white man can do no wrong. They are all to God as Sodom and Gomorrah.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” These pastors are wicked as hell. They are about nothing but money; they support wickedness, the fake Israelis and the falsehood called democracy. But the question is: who are the sheep of God's pasture?

Christ answers it: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” The sheep is the house of Israel. The sheep are not all nations on the planet: not the white man, not the Arab man, not the Chinese man. The only sheep are the twelve tribes of Israel.

So when you hear pastors say God is gathering his sheep and they are talking about Baptists, Catholics, Episcopalians and Anglicans, they have it all wrong. The pastors have destroyed and scattered the sheep, which is the house of Israel. “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: some pastors are Baptist and take one group of our people, some are African Methodist Episcopal and take another group, some are Catholic and take another. That is how they scatter God's flock and drive them away from the knowledge of the one true God, and God says, “behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings”.

precepts.text: Every plant which my heavenly Father hath not planted shall be rooted up. Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind, and both shall fall into the ditch. If the lying churches will not repent, leave them alone.
precepts.point: I have seen in the prophets of Jerusalem an horrible thing: they commit adultery, walk in lies, and strengthen the hands of evildoers, that none doth return from his wickedness. When Jamal Bryant was checked over his wife's dress he doubled down, so when we tell his congregants on the street to repent, they double down too. They are all to God as Sodom, and he will feed them wormwood and gall.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
The prophets of Jerusalem “strengthen also the hands of evildoers, that none doth return from his wickedness”. When Jamal Bryant was checked over his wife's dress, he did not say the Bible does say a woman should dress modestly, I was in error, I repent. He doubled down: I ain't wrong. So when we see his congregants on the street and say, sis, you can't wear pants, brother, you can't sell drugs, they double down just like him. That is the evil example. None return from their wickedness; they say the Lord did away with that, you twisted the scripture.

Christ cut the Pharisees the same way. His disciples said, “Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?” He answered, “Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.” These pastors, these so-called men of the cloth, have to go; they will be rooted up.

“Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.” The pastor and the congregation both fall. So leave these lying churches alone. If they will not repent, leave them alone. God says of them, “they are all of them unto me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah”, and he “will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink the water of gall”.

precepts.text: Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind, and both shall fall into the ditch.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ said of the Pharisees: “Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind.” Leave them alone. “And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch”: snared and trapped.

In Matthew 23 Christ cursed them out the whole chapter: “Woe unto you, ye blind guides”. Keep that in mind: blinded, blind, eyes darkened, eyes shut. They say whosoever swears by the temple it is nothing, but whosoever swears by the gold of the temple is a debtor: they worry about money, hearts “exercised with covetous practices” as Peter says. “Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?”

The same blind leaders are around today, dark clothes, a dark spirit. That is why we do not come together with other camps: different doctrines, and some of those doctrines can lead you to damnation. Leaders of other camps who show up at our schools unannounced and then throw a tantrum on video for views show their real color. We don't show up at your house unannounced; there are channels, and you call first. A GMS member sat in one of our schools for months living a double life. We pray brothers get it right, but we let the blind leaders alone and keep doing the work.

precepts.text: Christ was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
precepts.point: God is raising that kingdom now as Israel repents and learns who it is.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
Daniel says the secret was revealed not for any wisdom of his own, “but for their sakes that shall make known the interpretation to the king”, and the interpretation is the kingdom: the stone cut out without hands breaks the image of gold, silver, brass, iron and clay, and “in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed”. God is raising up that kingdom right now, and it is being built among the people Christ came for.

Christ says who those people are: “But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Christ only came for the lost sheep, and we are the lost sheep. Christ came to die for us, brothers; that was the purpose, to redeem us back to the Father.

So never think that we are not special. Christ did not come to die for everybody. He only died for the Israelites, so he could bring us back to the Father, and from there the kingdom is set up.

That is what you see right now: we are repenting and starting to know who we are, Judah, Benjamin, Levi, Ephraim, Simeon, coming out of that filthy Christian church, stopping the stealing and the adultery. In the middle of waking up you are going to make mistakes, but when you do, don't stay down; repent, rise back up and keep it moving, because you are the chosen. This world is darkness, and we are the light of this world. Don't turn that light off and go back to darkness; darkness has nothing to offer you but death.

precepts.text: Christ, sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, called the woman of another nation a dog, and she said, Truth, Lord.
precepts.point: Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
Christ shows who the dogs are. “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” A woman of another nation came and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me, and he answered, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs. And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”

Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord. The children are Israel, the lost sheep he was sent to; the dogs are the other nations. So the price of a dog that may not come into the house of the Lord is not about a four-legged animal.

precepts.text: Like the woman who answered, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table, and Christ said, great is thy faith; Rahab is a heathen whose faith the Lord honoured.
precepts.point: Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to the roof and confessed: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is faith and belief; a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land.

note.label: Joshua 2: Rahab and the Spies

precepts.why:
Rahab is a heathen, yet she says, “I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us”. That is faith and belief: a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land. She is like the woman who answered Christ, “Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.” “Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt.”

That woman knew her place and still believed, and Christ honoured it. Rahab knew the Lord had given Israel the land, believed it, and put her life on the line for it, and the Lord honoured her faith the same way.

precepts.text: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel; it is not meet to take the children's bread and to cast it to dogs; Christ called the other nations dogs just as Exodus 11:7 and Joshua 10:21 do.
precepts.point: Christ did not come for all nations; he came for one people. If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
Christ called the other nations dogs just as Exodus 11:7 and Joshua 10:21 do: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” And when the woman worshipped him and said, “Lord, help me”, he answered, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.”

Christ did not come for all nations; he came for one people. If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised. The dogs of Exodus, the dogs of Joshua, and the dogs Christ spoke of are the nations, and the Lord put a difference between them and Israel.

precepts.text: Christ said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the woman answered, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table; because she acknowledged who he is, who she is, and who the children of Israel are, he said, O woman, great is thy faith, and her daughter was made whole.
precepts.point: Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Ruth cleaved to Naomi: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God. Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same.

Christ said, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” The woman worshipped him and said, “Lord, help me.” He answered, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” And she said, “Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”

She acknowledged who he is, who she is, and who the children of Israel are. Because of that he said, “O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.” That is the place Ruth took: under Israel, with Israel's God as her God.

precepts.text: The Canaanite woman was healed only when she owned herself a dog and submitted under Israel; that faith moved Him.
precepts.point: The Most High hears the stranger who submits and fears Him, so all nations know the name attached to this house. He does not honor a prayer prayed against Israel or for dominion over His people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 6: Solomon's Prayer of Dedication

precepts.why:
Christ told the Canaanite woman, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” She did not fight it. She said, “Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.” She owned herself a dog and submitted under Israel, and that faith moved him: “O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.”

That is the stranger Solomon prayed for, “which is not of thy people Israel, but is come from a far country for thy great name’s sake.” The Most High hears the stranger who submits and fears him, “that all people of the earth may know thy name, and fear thee, as doth thy people Israel.”

He does not honor a prayer prayed against Israel or for dominion over his people. The stranger is heard in the place of the dog under the master’s table, not in the place of the children.

precepts.text: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel; the lost sheep are the house of Israel.
precepts.point: Let my soul live, and it shall praise Thee, and let Thy judgments help me. I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Thy servant, for I do not forget Thy commandments. The lost sheep is the house of Israel, the people who go astray and must seek the face of the Most High early and follow this Bible, fleeing the strange doctrines.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
Christ says, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” The lost sheep are the house of Israel. So when David says “I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I do not forget thy commandments”, that is Israel, the people who go astray and must seek the face of the Most High early.

That is who this whole cry belongs to: “Let my cry come near before thee, O Lord: give me understanding according to thy word.”

precepts.text: Christ says He was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, yet Christianity answers with John 3:16.
precepts.point: With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people; off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law the oppressor's culture was beaten into them until they came to understand. This Bible is the rest and the refreshing, yet they would not hear, so the word came precept upon precept that they might fall backward and be broken and snared.

note.label: Isaiah 28: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim and Precept Upon Precept

precepts.why:
Precept upon precept is how the puzzle is put together, and here is how it is torn apart. Christ says plainly, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” That is who he was sent to, the lost sheep of the house of Israel and no one else.

Yet Christianity answers that with John 3:16, as if it cancels what Christ said of himself. That is not laying a scripture upon a scripture; that is using one verse to fight another. The Bible is a puzzle in the Old and New Testaments, and the pieces must be put together, not set against each other. Christ’s own words about who he was sent to stand.

precepts.text: The same account told in Matthew: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders?
precepts.point: There is no law in the scriptures that a man must wash his hands before he eats. That was a tradition of the elders, and the whole contention is about tradition, not about law.

note.label: Mark 7: The Tradition of the Elders and What Defiles a Man

precepts.why:
The Pharisees and scribes saw some of the disciples eat bread “with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.” They asked, “Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?”

Matthew tells the same account and puts the charge the same way: “Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” Notice the word in both: tradition. There is no law in the scriptures that a man must wash his hands before he eats. That was a tradition of the elders, and the whole contention is about tradition, not about law. The Pharisees themselves named it a transgression of the tradition of the elders, not of the law.

precepts.text: "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel," identifying who the lost are.
precepts.point: To fit the other nations into this as the gentiles who are grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. The scriptures show the opposite: the nations are the ones who did the stealing and the hiding, so they are not the gentiles being restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Christ identifies who the lost are: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

The Son of man came to save that which was lost, and the lost are the house of Israel. So the restitution of all things is Israel's, the people who lost their kingdom and their heritage, not the nations who never lost anything.

precepts.text: The woman of Canaan cried, and Christ answered, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
precepts.point: Read logically, using comparison and context. Christianity teaches people to read the bible with a slave mind, taking a verse at face value the way the slave master intended, instead of going back to the beginning as you would with any book or film.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
When a real Greek came to Christ, the response was the opposite. “And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou Son of David”. She called him Son of David to disassociate her race from his.

“But he answered her not a word.” Christ ignored her, let the disciples say, “Send her away; for she crieth after us”, and then said plainly, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

The Greeks of John 12 never had to go through that; Christ answered them with prophecy. The difference is that they were Israelites and she was not.
